instructions.question: What overall sentiment does the tweet's author express, judging by their attitude, mood or evaluation rather than the topic alone?
instructions.rule: Label by the author's own feeling: excitement, praise, anticipation, well-wishes or promotional enthusiasm count as positive even with swearing; complaints, disappointment, mockery, sarcasm, insults or sadness count as negative even when mild or joking. Plain news, announcements, questions, factual statements, sales listings and ambiguous jokes with no clear stance are neutral. A hedged or playful remark without a clear evaluation stays neutral.

neutral.what: Informational headlines, announcements, questions, factual sports/poll reports, ticket sales, or offhand remarks without a clear positive or negative stance.
examples: CNN/ORC Poll: Donald Trump takes the top slot in Iowa, Scott Walker falls to 3rd. Ben Carson in 2nd
@user What happened at the Spurs game last night mate?
Selling a ticket for Twilight Sad at the Barrowlands this Saturday (Face value)
I'm not sure what Rahul Gandhi is trying to accomplish with all of this
neutral.cues: news-style phrasing, question marks, may, find out, watch out, dates/times, retweet if, who do you think
neutral.not_for: Questions or reports that clearly complain or mock are negative; announcements with exclamatory hype are positive.

positive.what: Author shows enthusiasm, praise, anticipation, gratitude, condolences/blessings, or upbeat promotion of an event or product.
examples: Living for Magic Mike XXL with @user tomorrow.
noel fielding may be one of the greatest people alive.
Sending my sincere prayers & condolences to the Gifford family on Frank Gifford's passing. May he rest in peace.
Tomorrow, Apple Inc. will introduce the 6S, a new Apple TV and the iPad Pro.
positive.cues: can't wait, so excited, best, happy, love, great, yasssss, bring on, may the force be with you, blessings, !!
positive.not_for: Event ads or schedules written flatly with no excitement are neutral; sympathy news reports without the author's wishes are neutral.

negative.what: Author complains, criticizes, mocks, is disappointed, annoyed, sad, bored, or attacks a person or group, including sarcasm.
examples: Dream High 2 sucks compared to the 1st one.
Very disappointed to learn that the Great Yorkshire Show has been cancelled @user . Had planned to go tomorrow.
The best way to find Malaysia Airlines Flight MH370 may be with Michelle Obama's arms.
they were talking about the teen awards on Sunday and they mentioned ashton being sick :(
negative.cues: sucks, disappointed, bored, despise, sad, can't go, missed, stop whining, fail, :(, #sarcasm, c'mon
negative.not_for: Swearing used for excitement is positive; joking boasts with no complaint are neutral.
